playGuides.title: Calling for checks
playGuides.intro: Call for a check only when failure is interesting and the outcome uncertain. Set the DC before the dice land: use a simple DC for the task's proficiency (untrained 10, trained 15, expert 20, master 30, legendary 40) or the level-based DC for the threat. Every roll has four outcomes: decide what a critical success and a critical failure look like, not only pass or fail.

tips.text: No roll when there is time and no cost to retrying: the character succeeds, given time.
Read all four degrees. A critical success should feel like more than a success (extra information, extra time, an advantage for the next roll); a critical failure costs something more than a failure.
Fortune and misfortune (roll twice, keep the higher or lower) are for special effects; for a good plan or bad footing use +2 or −2 circumstance modifiers instead.
A natural 20 improves the result one step and a natural 1 worsens it one step: a natural 20 that misses the DC by 3 is still a success.
Use Perception for initiative unless the characters were already doing something: sneaking rolls Stealth, talking rolls Deception or Diplomacy.
Recall Knowledge is a free action economy for curious players: answer one useful question on a success, two on a critical success.

groups.label: Awareness
groups.summary: Noticing, tracking and reading a situation before it reads you.

groups.label: Physical
groups.summary: Moving, climbing, grappling and keeping your feet.

groups.label: Social
groups.summary: Changing what other people do or believe.

groups.label: Subterfuge
groups.summary: Staying unseen and getting past locks and traps.

groups.label: Saving throws
groups.summary: Resisting what the world does to you.

entries.label: Perception
entries.summary: Spotting, hearing, sensing motives; also what most characters roll for initiative.
callFor: something moves at the edge of the torchlight
a door that should be locked stands ajar
the host's smile slips for a moment
entries.success: They notice it in time to act on it: name the detail and what it suggests.
entries.failure: They miss it, or notice it only as it happens. Do not hide the whole adventure behind one Perception roll.
examples: Roll Perception: what do you see in the rafters?
Roll Perception for initiative; the ambush is already moving.

entries.label: Fortitude
entries.summary: Poison, disease, exhaustion, and effects that test the body.
callFor: a poisoned blade
a day's march through the burning plain
a cloud of spores
entries.success: They shrug off the worst of it; describe the near miss.
entries.failure: It takes hold; make the cost visible on the sheet and in the scene.

entries.label: Reflex
entries.summary: Dodging blasts, traps and falling rocks.
callFor: a fireball
the floor giving way
a scything blade from the wall
entries.success: They dive clear, or take only part of it.
entries.failure: Caught: they take it in full, and maybe end up prone.

entries.label: Will
entries.summary: Fear, charms, illusions and mental attacks.
callFor: a dragon's frightful presence
a voice that commands obedience
an illusion that seems too real
entries.success: Their mind stays their own; let them see the trick for what it is.
entries.failure: The fear or the charm lands; play it, then let them fight it next turn.

entries.label: Acrobatics
entries.summary: Balance, tumbling, squeezing and acrobatic flying.
callFor: a narrow beam over a drop
slipping past a foe's guard
a rope bridge in high wind
entries.success: They are where they wanted to be, with the next move open.
entries.failure: They stall or slip; a critical failure means a fall or a foe's free swing.

entries.label: Arcana
entries.summary: Arcane magic, constructs, magical theory and arcane creatures.
callFor: a glowing sigil on a vault door
a construct that will not stop
a wizard's coded notes
entries.success: Name what it is and one useful way to deal with it.
entries.failure: They know what it is, not how it ends; a critical failure gives a confident wrong answer.

entries.label: Athletics
entries.summary: Climbing, jumping, swimming, and every grapple, shove and trip.
callFor: a cliff with a deadline
a river in flood
pinning the cultist before they finish the chant
entries.success: Fast and clean: give them the position or the grip they wanted.
entries.failure: They make little headway, tire, or end up in a worse spot.

entries.label: Crafting
entries.summary: Making, repairing and understanding how things are built.
callFor: a broken axle on the road
a lock's mechanism under a spotlight
copying a key from a wax impression
entries.success: It works, and they understand how; give them a fact about the maker.
entries.failure: It takes longer, costs more, or works once and then fails.

entries.label: Deception
entries.summary: Lies, feints, disguises and impersonation.
callFor: a forged pass at the gate
a feint before the real strike
pretending to belong at the ball
entries.success: The lie holds for now; decide what would break it.
entries.failure: Doubt creeps in: a follow-up question, a guard sent to check.

entries.label: Diplomacy
entries.summary: Making an impression, asking for help, gathering information.
callFor: asking a stranger for directions to the ruin
talking the mob down
a favor from the harbor master
entries.success: Their attitude improves, or they agree to a reasonable request.
entries.failure: No, or not yet: a price, a condition, or a task first.

entries.label: Intimidation
entries.summary: Coercing and demoralizing.
callFor: a thug who should back down
an informant holding out
a battle cry to break the line
entries.success: They comply or are frightened, now. Fear has a long memory.
entries.failure: They call the bluff, get angry, or go for help.

entries.label: Medicine
entries.summary: First aid, treating wounds and diseases, reading a body.
callFor: a friend bleeding out mid-fight
a sickness spreading in the village
how long the body has been here
entries.success: Stable, treated or dated: give them a hard, useful fact.
entries.failure: Time passes without progress; on a critical failure the patient is hurt.

entries.label: Nature
entries.summary: Animals, plants, weather, terrain and primal magic.
callFor: which mushrooms are safe
tracks of something heavy
a druid's circle of standing stones
entries.success: They know what it is and what it means for them right now.
entries.failure: They know the common case; this one is different.

entries.label: Occultism
entries.summary: Strange philosophies, aberrations, spirits and occult magic.
callFor: a haunting that repeats every night
a sigil that hurts to look at
a medium's séance gone wrong
entries.success: Name the pattern and what the spirit or creature wants.
entries.failure: They recognize the shape of it but not its rules.

entries.label: Performance
entries.summary: Music, acting, oratory; earning coin and attention.
callFor: earning a meal at the inn
distracting a crowd while a friend works
a festival contest
entries.success: The audience is theirs: coin, attention, or a useful admirer.
entries.failure: Polite silence, a heckler, or a rival who now wants to compete.

entries.label: Religion
entries.summary: Faiths, rites, divine magic and undead.
callFor: an unfamiliar shrine
a priest's oddly worded blessing
an undead that ignores holy water
entries.success: Name the rite, the faith's customs or the creature's weakness.
entries.failure: They know the faith, but miss that this is a heresy of it.

entries.label: Society
entries.summary: Customs, law, history, etiquette and forgeries.
callFor: a noble's crest on a ring
a law that makes no sense
a letter that is almost right
entries.success: Give them the custom, the person, or the flaw in the forgery.
entries.failure: They recall the popular version, which is wrong in one way that matters.

entries.label: Stealth
entries.summary: Hiding, sneaking and avoiding notice while travelling.
callFor: slipping past sentries
following someone through the market
approaching the camp before dawn
entries.success: They are unnoticed, and where they want to be.
entries.failure: Spotted at the worst moment, or they must choose: retreat or go loud.

entries.label: Survival
entries.summary: Tracking, finding the way, living off the land.
callFor: the trail splits at a stream
supplies run short two days from town
a storm is coming over the ridge
entries.success: They find the trail, the shelter or the food, and gain time.
entries.failure: They lose time, a day's rations, or arrive somewhere other than planned.

entries.label: Thievery
entries.summary: Picking locks, disabling devices, stealing and palming.
callFor: a lock with guards on patrol
a trap's trigger plate
lifting a key from a belt
entries.success: Done, quietly, and nobody saw.
entries.failure: Not done yet; on a critical failure the trap triggers or someone saw.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.prompt: The pitch: what kind of adventures these are and why the party is together.

sections.title: The world
sections.prompt: Your world in a few paragraphs: the region where play begins, who rules it, its gods and magic, and what has gone wrong lately.

sections.title: What everyone knows
sections.prompt: Legends, recent events, rumours from the road and anything a commoner would know. Keep the secrets for play.

sections.title: Places and factions you've heard of
sections.prompt: Settlements, ruins and roads, and the guilds, orders and powers the characters know by name, one line each.

sections.title: House rules
sections.prompt: Variant rules you use (free archetype, automatic bonus progression, proficiency without level) and table habits.

sections.title: Making your character
sections.prompt: Starting level, which ancestries, heritages, backgrounds, classes and rarities are allowed, and how the party knows each other.
sections.starter:
- **Options**: common ancestries, heritages, backgrounds and classes; ask before anything uncommon or rare
- **Ability boosts**: as the core rules give them
- **Bring**: a reason to adventure and a tie to one other character

sections.title: Where we begin
sections.prompt: Where the party is when the first session starts, and the trouble that brings them together.

conditions.summary: Can't see: all normal terrain is difficult terrain, it detects nothing by vision and critically fails Perception checks that need sight; −4 status to Perception if vision is its only precise sense. Immune to visual effects; overrides dazzled.
manual: −4 status to Perception when vision is its only precise sense
flat checks to target creatures it can't see
conditions.name: Blinded

conditions.summary: Objects only: a broken item can't be used for its normal function and grants no bonuses, except armor, which keeps its item bonus to AC but takes a −1 to −3 status penalty to AC by category.
conditions.name: Broken

conditions.summary: A status penalty equal to the value to Dexterity-based rolls and DCs: AC, Reflex saves, ranged attack rolls, and Acrobatics, Stealth and Thievery checks.
conditions.name: Clumsy

conditions.summary: Hard to see (fog, dim light): anyone targeting it with an attack, spell or other effect must succeed at a DC 5 flat check or it fails to affect it. Area effects ignore this.
manual: the DC 5 flat check to target it
conditions.name: Concealed

conditions.summary: Off-guard; treats no one as an ally; can't Delay, Ready or use reactions; spends its actions on Strikes or offensive cantrips against random targets. Each time it takes damage from an attack or spell, a DC 11 flat check ends it.
manual: the DC 11 flat check when damaged
conditions.name: Confused

conditions.summary: Its will is subverted: the controller decides what it does, including its reactions and whether it Delays.
conditions.name: Controlled

conditions.summary: Oracles only: the oracular curse tightens, with effects that depend on the value. Only Refocusing removes it.
manual: the curse's effects at each value
conditions.name: Cursebound

conditions.summary: Vision swimming: if vision is its only precise sense, every creature and object is concealed from it (DC 5 flat check to target).
manual: the DC 5 flat check to target
conditions.name: Dazzled

conditions.summary: Can't hear: critically fails Perception checks that need hearing; −2 status to initiative and to Perception checks involving sound; auditory actions need a DC 5 flat check. Immune to auditory effects.
manual: −2 status to initiative and sound-based Perception
the DC 5 flat check for auditory actions
conditions.name: Deafened

conditions.summary: Its soul is drawn toward death: it dies at dying 4 minus the doomed value (the sheet's dying maximum). Drops by 1 after each full night's rest.
manual: death at the lower dying value
conditions.name: Doomed

conditions.summary: A status penalty equal to the value to Constitution-based rolls and DCs, such as Fortitude saves. It also loses Hit Points and maximum Hit Points equal to its level (at least 1) times the value. Drops by 1 after a full night's rest.
manual: the lost Hit Points and maximum Hit Points
conditions.name: Drained

conditions.summary: Bleeding out and unconscious. A recovery check at the start of each of its turns (DC 10 + dying) makes it better or worse; damage raises it by 1 (2 from a critical hit or a critical failure). Dying 4 is death (less when doomed). Healed to 1 Hit Point or more, it loses dying; losing dying gives wounded 1 (or 1 more).
manual: recovery checks at the start of its turn
wounded when it ends by a recovery check
conditions.name: Dying

conditions.summary: Carrying more than it can manage: clumsy 1 and a 10-foot penalty to all its Speeds (never below 5 feet).
conditions.name: Encumbered

conditions.summary: A status penalty equal to the value to Strength-based rolls and DCs, including Strength-based melee attack and damage rolls and Athletics checks.
conditions.name: Enfeebled

conditions.summary: Focused on something: −2 status to Perception and skill checks, and no concentrate actions unrelated to the subject. Ends if anyone acts with hostility against it or its allies.
conditions.name: Fascinated

conditions.summary: Tired: −1 status to AC and saving throws, and no exploration activities while traveling. A full night's rest ends it.
conditions.name: Fatigued

conditions.summary: Must spend its actions getting away from the source as fast as it can; can't Delay or Ready.
conditions.name: Fleeing

conditions.summary: Attitude: likes the character and agrees to simple, safe Requests. Hostile actions worsen it.
conditions.name: Friendly

conditions.summary: A status penalty equal to the value to all its checks and DCs (AC included). Drops by 1 at the end of each of its turns.
conditions.name: Frightened

conditions.summary: Held in place by another creature: off-guard and immobilized. A manipulate action needs a DC 5 flat check or it is lost.
manual: the DC 5 flat check for manipulate actions
conditions.name: Grabbed

conditions.summary: Attitude: wants to help the character and accepts reasonable Requests. Hostile actions worsen it.
conditions.name: Helpful

conditions.summary: Others know its space but not exactly where it is: they are off-guard to it, and must succeed at a DC 11 flat check to target it. Area effects ignore this.
manual: the DC 11 flat check to target it
conditions.name: Hidden

conditions.summary: Attitude: seeks to harm the character and won't accept Requests.
conditions.name: Hostile

conditions.summary: Can't use actions with the move trait; forcing it out of its space takes a check against what holds it.
conditions.name: Immobilized

conditions.summary: Attitude: doesn't care either way about the character (the default).
conditions.name: Indifferent

conditions.summary: Can't be seen: undetected by everyone (hidden to anyone who already saw it, until it Sneaks). Others can Seek to find it.
manual: being undetected or hidden to each creature
conditions.name: Invisible

conditions.summary: In plain view of a creature's precise sense: the normal state.
manual: the normal state; nothing to apply
conditions.name: Observed

conditions.summary: Distracted: −2 circumstance penalty to AC.
conditions.name: Off-Guard

conditions.summary: Frozen in place: off-guard; can't act except to Recall Knowledge and use purely mental actions; its senses work only where it can perceive without moving.
manual: purely mental actions are still allowed
conditions.name: Paralyzed

conditions.summary: Takes the noted damage at the end of each of its turns, rolled anew, then a DC 15 flat check ends it.
manual: rolling the damage at the end of its turn
the DC 15 flat check to end it
conditions.name: Persistent Damage

conditions.summary: Turned to stone: can't act or sense anything. It is an object (AC 9, Hardness 8, Bulk doubled) with the Hit Points it had; if the statue is destroyed, it dies.
conditions.name: Petrified

conditions.summary: Lying down: off-guard and −2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls; can only Crawl or Stand (standing ends it). Taking Cover while prone gives +4 circumstance AC against ranged attacks.
conditions.name: Prone

conditions.summary: Gains 1 extra action at the start of each turn, often limited to certain actions by the effect.
conditions.name: Quickened

conditions.summary: Tied up or pinned: off-guard and immobilized; no attack or manipulate actions except to Escape or Force Open. Overrides grabbed.
manual: only Escape or Force Open among attack and manipulate actions
conditions.name: Restrained

conditions.summary: A status penalty equal to the value to all its checks and DCs; it can't willingly ingest anything. Retching (an action) allows a Fortitude save to reduce it by 1 (2 on a critical success).
conditions.name: Sickened

conditions.summary: Regains that many fewer actions at the start of each of its turns.
conditions.name: Slowed

conditions.summary: Can't act. It loses that many actions as it regains them (the value drops by the actions lost), or all its actions for a duration. Overrides slowed.
manual: actions lost and the value going down
conditions.name: Stunned

conditions.summary: A status penalty equal to the value to Intelligence-, Wisdom- and Charisma-based rolls and DCs: Will saves, spell attacks and spell DCs, and those skills. Casting a spell needs a flat check (DC 5 + value) or the spell is disrupted.
manual: the flat check to cast a spell
spell attack rolls and spell DCs
conditions.name: Stupefied

conditions.summary: Asleep or knocked out: can't act; −4 status to AC, Perception and Reflex saves; blinded and off-guard; falls prone and drops what it holds. Healed to 1 Hit Point or more, it wakes.
conditions.name: Unconscious

conditions.summary: Others can't see it or tell which space it is in: they are off-guard to it, and can only guess a square (a DC 11 flat check, rolled in secret) or Seek.
conditions.name: Undetected

conditions.summary: Attitude: dislikes and distrusts the character and won't accept Requests.
conditions.name: Unfriendly

conditions.summary: Others have no idea it is there; it is also undetected.
conditions.name: Unnoticed

conditions.summary: Seriously injured: when it gains dying, the dying value goes up by the wounded value. Ends after Treat Wounds restores Hit Points, or at full Hit Points after 10 minutes of rest.
manual: ending with Treat Wounds or rest
conditions.name: Wounded

zeroHp.text: At 0 Hit Points a character is dying 1 (dying 2 from a critical hit or a critical failure) plus its wounded value, and unconscious. It makes a recovery check at the start of each turn (DC 10 + dying); damage while dying raises it by 1 (2 on a critical); dying 4 (less when doomed) is death. Healed to 1 Hit Point or more, it loses dying and unconscious, and its wounded value goes up by 1.
zeroHp.cite: Player Core — Hit Points, Healing, and Dying

zeroHp.text: A creature or hazard at 0 Hit Points dies or is destroyed (an attacker can knock a creature out instead with a nonlethal attack).
zeroHp.cite: Player Core — Hit Points, Healing, and Dying

blocks.title: Cover
blocks.text: **Lesser cover** (a creature in the way): +1 circumstance bonus to AC. **Standard cover**: +2 circumstance bonus to AC, to Reflex saves against area effects and to Stealth checks to Hide or Sneak. **Greater cover**: +4 to the same.

classNotes.alchemist: Alchemist: record your formula book and the versatile vials and Quick Alchemy you prepare.
classNotes.cleric: Cleric: choose your deity and divine font with the GM (the module suggests no deities).
classNotes.champion: Champion: choose your deity and sanctification with the GM, and your blessing at 3rd level.
classNotes.druid: Druid: note your anathema and, for an animal order, your animal companion.
classNotes.witch: Witch: record your familiar's abilities and your patron's hexes.
classNotes.wizard: Wizard: record your spellbook and your arcane bond item.

pf2e-orc-books.animist: Animist: choose your apparitions and their spells by hand.
pf2e-orc-books.commander: Commander: note your banner and which tactics you have prepared.
pf2e-orc-books.exemplar: Exemplar: note which ikons hold your divine spark; epithets after 3rd level are chosen by hand when the builder does not offer them.
pf2e-orc-books.guardian: Guardian: record your guardian's armor and techniques.
pf2e-orc-books.gunslinger: Gunslinger: note your deeds and your slinger's reload.
pf2e-orc-books.inventor: Inventor: build your innovation's modifications (armor, construct, weapon or mortar) by hand.
pf2e-orc-books.magus: Magus: prepare your spells and studious spells by hand.

steps.title: Attribute boosts
steps.intro: Four free boosts to four different attributes, after ancestry, background and class.
guide: The remaster writes attribute modifiers, not scores: every boost adds 1.
No source boosts one attribute twice, so a 1st-level modifier is at most +4.
Your class's key attribute should usually be your highest.

steps.title: Skills and languages

guide: A skill your background and class both train counts once: you pick another instead (the count includes it).

templates.name: One-shot in three acts
templates.description: A single evening: a hook that starts in motion, a middle that complicates it, and a finale with a clear win or loss.

scaffold.title: One-shot
scaffold.premise: Who needs help, what goes wrong if nobody acts, and why tonight?
scaffold.playerIntro: Start mid-scene: the characters already know each other and already have a reason to act.
scaffold.gmSituation: Write the villain's plan in three steps; each act the party fails to stop one, the next one happens.

acts.title: The hook
acts.goal: Get the party moving within ten minutes of play.
acts.pacing: One short encounter (a low threat), then a choice of two ways forward.

scenes.purpose: Open on trouble: an attack, a theft, a plea for help.
A quick social scene to learn what is at stake and who to trust.

acts.title: Complications
acts.goal: The obvious plan meets the villain's first step.
acts.pacing: Alternate exploration with one moderate encounter; keep each under an hour.

scenes.purpose: A place to explore with a hazard and a clue to the finale.
A fight against the villain's minions; let the terrain matter.

acts.title: Finale
acts.goal: Face the villain where it matters, with the clock almost out.
acts.pacing: One severe encounter with a goal besides defeating everything.

scenes.purpose: The showdown, and a minute of epilogue for each character.

scaffold.epilogue: Tell each player one thing their character changed.

templates.name: A short delve
templates.description: A location-based adventure: rumours lead to a lair, the lair pushes back with creatures and hazards, the aftermath sets up the next session.

scaffold.title: A short delve
scaffold.premise: Something has made its home nearby, and the people next door are paying for it.

acts.title: Rumours
acts.goal: Learn where the lair is and one thing about its master.

scenes.purpose: Witnesses disagree about what they saw (Recall Knowledge and Diplomacy).
The road there: a low-threat encounter from the encounter builder.

acts.title: The lair
acts.goal: Get past a hazard, a guardian and a puzzle to the heart of the lair.

scenes.purpose: Entrance: a simple hazard that rewards Searching.
A setback or a twist: an unexpected ally, prisoner or rival.
The master of the lair, on its own ground (a severe threat).

acts.title: Aftermath
acts.goal: Treasure, consequences and a new rumour.

scenes.purpose: Return to the people who suffered; something has changed while they were away.

scaffold.purpose: Someone has what the party needs and wants something in return.
scaffold.body:
- Their attitude now (hostile to helpful), and what would move it one step.
- What will they never agree to?
- What happens if the talk fails?
- Which checks fit: Perception (Sense Motive), Diplomacy, Deception, Intimidation, a Lore.

scaffold.purpose: A fight with a reason and a way to end other than death.
scaffold.body:
- Threat and XP budget for this party (use the encounter builder).
- Terrain: one feature that offers cover, one that is difficult or hazardous.
- When do the foes flee or surrender?
- What is the reward for winning, and the cost of losing?

scaffold.purpose: A trap or a dangerous place that tests the party's caution.
scaffold.body:
- Stealth DC to notice it, and who is Searching.
- How to disable it, and which skill and proficiency it needs.
- What it does when triggered, and whether it rolls initiative (a complex hazard).
- What a clever party can do instead of disabling it.

items.text: Check each character's level, Hit Points, Focus Points and spell slots
items.guidance: Note who levelled up, who ended the session wounded, and who spent their Hero Points.
Use the encounter builder: pick the threat (low for warm-ups, moderate for most fights, severe for a boss) and the party's level and size.

items.text: Have three names and one quirk ready
items.guidance: Roll the NPC generator once or twice so improvised characters do not all sound alike.

items.text: Give each character 1 Hero Point at the start, more for heroics
items.guidance: The Hero Points tracker keeps count; a character can hold up to 3.
The Initiative tracker rolls d20 plus Perception (or the skill a character was using) and sorts highest first.

items.text: Clear conditions and note wounded and doomed values
items.guidance: Wounded goes away with a full rest or Treat Wounds; doomed drops by 1 after a full night's rest.
A character levels up at 1,000 XP and keeps the rest.

items.text: Record treasure and who carries it (and their Bulk)

templates.name: Session zero
templates.description: Settle expectations before the first session; answers go into campaign settings.

items.text: What tone are we going for?
Which topics are off the table, and which should fade to black?
Starting level, and experience or milestone advancement?
Which character options are allowed (common only, or uncommon with a reason)?
Any variant or house rules (free archetype, automatic bonuses, critical cards)?
Why does this party stick together?

styleNotes: Heroic fantasy with teeth: describe the world vividly, set DCs before the dice land, and give all four degrees of success a meaning.
ORC core-rules text is used as written, without the publisher's setting names; GM advice, tables and generators marked Original are Campaign Forge's own.
